# ParseUrlFailureDereferenced

<Badge type="warning" text="warning" /> <Badge type="tip" text="on by default" />

Group: [Probable bugs](/rules/#probable-bugs)

Identify ordinary unguarded reads of dynamic parse_url results, or literal results with a supported parsing-failure proof. Restrict to array-returning mode; missing keys are another concern.

## Detection

A resolved same-file reference parameter, reference capture or global writer
can replace a checked result. Retain the producer of that replacement while
clearing the earlier binding proof. Giving an element to an unresolved method
does not rebind the containing array.

Follow each producer reaching a local read, including results written on an
earlier loop turn or before a backward jump. A check of an earlier result does
not check a later replacement; a check repeated before every consumption does.
Ignore producers belonging to other result contracts when selecting an
unchecked result.

- D1. Report ordinary unguarded reads of dynamic parse_url results, or literal results with a supported parsing-failure proof. Empty HTTP(S) authorities and ports above 65535 establish such a proof. Restrict to array-returning mode; missing keys are another concern.
- D2. Resolve builtin functions, classes, constants and methods, including imports and supported named arguments. Follow only bounded local facts within one lexical scope. Receiver and argument provenance must establish the specific API contract; variable names and comments never prove intent.
- D3. Report one finding per violating operation. A reachable path, unchanged value identity and applicable API behavior are required. Intervening mutation, unknown calls involving tracked values, escaped aliases or exhausted analysis budgets invalidate proof.
- D3a. When several assignments reach the read (a loop that reassigns the variable, or an assignment made on one path only), the read is reported if one of them is a result of this API that no guard on its own path covers. A guard written before the other assignment does not cover it; a test inside the loop, or after the conditional assignment, covers every assignment. A reaching value that is not a result of this API (a literal, another call, an unknown value) never causes a report by itself. It does not hide one either: an unguarded result of another call reaching the same read leaves a result of this API reported.
- D3b. A result assigned inside a condition (`if (($parts = parse_url($raw)) === false) { … }`) is tracked like one assigned in its own statement. Only the conditions of D4 guard it: an operator whose outcome does not fix the comparison (`xor`, `^`, a comparison between two conditions) proves nothing, and neither does a branch that does not exit. `|` and `&` between two tests evaluate both: the comparison is fixed where `|` yields false and where `&` yields true, and nowhere else.
- D4. A read is guarded when a condition on the same variable, written after the producing call and before any reassignment, excludes `false` on every path to the read. Accepted condition shapes:
  - strict or loose comparison with `false` (`$parts === false`, `false != $parts`);
  - plain truthiness (`$parts`, `!$parts`) and `empty($parts)`;
  - `is_array($parts)` and `array_key_exists($key, $parts)` resolved to the builtins;
  - `isset` or `empty` on a key of the variable (`isset($parts['host'])`, `!empty($parts['path'])`); `isset($parts)` alone proves nothing because `false` is set.
  - negation, and `&&`/`||` (also `and`/`or`) combinations: a true conjunction needs one proving operand, a false conjunction needs all of them, and symmetrically for disjunctions.
- D5. A guard applies in these positions: the matching branch of an enclosing `if`/`elseif`/`else` (later branches also know the earlier conditions failed); the matching arm of an enclosing ternary; the right operand of `&&` or `||` whose left operand is the guard; and any statement after an earlier sibling `if` whose main body always exits, at every enclosing block level inside the same function scope.

Only completely followed same-file bodies export replacement producers.
An unstarted generator closure does not establish that its body wrote a new
result; advancing generators is outside this local producer contract.

## Exceptions (no report)

- Array and list destructuring destinations create slots rather than reading them. Destructuring keys and ordinary array values still require reads.

- Literal URL shapes outside the supported failure proof receive no finding. This avoids requesting runtime failure guards for constants whose parsing outcome is unsupported.

- Guarded probes with isset, empty or null coalescing, unsets and plain nested slot creation do not read a failed or missing value. Index expressions and the fallback operand of null coalescing still require normal reads.

- Reads guarded as described by D4 and D5 never index the failure value.
- A value the shared flow analysis proves is not false at the read is never reported, whatever form the proof takes: the conditions of D4 in the positions of D5, a loop condition, a statement that leaves on the failing outcome (`$parts !== false or exit;`, `$parts or throw …;`, `$parts ?: throw …;`), a failing branch that ends in a call that never returns (a callee declared `never`, or a function or a final or private method every path of which throws or exits), a test stored in a boolean and tested later while neither the boolean nor the tested variable has been written, and, on PHP 8.0 and later outside any `try` with a `catch`, a builtin call that returned after receiving the value for a parameter that only accepts arrays, objects or callables (`count($parts)` throws a `TypeError` for `false`; before PHP 8 it warns and returns, which proves nothing). A `switch (true)` case is read like the condition of an `if`/`elseif` chain; in a `switch` on the variable itself with constant labels, the cases after a `false` or `null` label and the `default` hold a value that is neither, as does a `true` case. Positions PHP may skip prove nothing: the right side of `??=`, the arguments of a null-safe call and anything chained after `?->`. A null-safe call to a never-returning method does not end the path, and `f(...)` creates a closure without calling `f`. An arm of `match (true)` is read like a `switch (true)` case; an arm that throws, exits or calls a function that never returns takes no part in what holds after the `match`. `|` and `&` between two tests are read like `||` and `&&` for the outcome that fixes both operands (a false `|`, a true `&`), and a strict `in_array($v, [...], true)` over literals that include neither `false` nor `null` excludes both where it holds. `goto` jumps are followed, except in a scope that also contains a `try`, which the flow analysis leaves alone. Where a `goto` label is written before the use, and after the place where its scope first names the checked variable, a variable that can hold the same value, or code that may write any variable (`extract`, `compact`, `get_defined_vars`, `parse_str` given one argument, a variable variable, `$GLOBALS`, `eval`, an included file), a jump can land between a guard and the use: only what the flow analysis establishes counts there, and a guard recognised by where it is written proves nothing. Two variables can hold the same value when one is written from the other by a plain assignment, an assignment by reference or `??=`, when a `foreach` takes one out of the other, or through a chain of those; in the value assigned, the receiver and the arguments of a call, the operands of an operator other than `??`, the variables a string embeds and an element key do not count, and a statement that only reads (`echo $prefix . $parts['host'];`) ties nothing. A parameter is named from the start of the function, and a checked expression that reads `$this` or no variable counts every label before it. In a scope the flow analysis does not follow (one that also contains a `try`, a generator, a scope that evaluates or includes code) a guarded use after such a label is therefore reported. A label written before all of that, such as a `retry:` label ahead of the `try` that produces and checks the value, changes nothing, whatever else the function reads beside the checked value; at file level every label written before the use counts. What was established of a `static` local holds until the next call, or code that runs without a call being written (an object converted to text, a magic property or offset access, the destructor of an object a variable held when it is given another value), that may enter the function again and assign the variable. A call of PHP's own counts as such when it may run code of the project: it is given a callback other than the name of a PHP function that only computes on text and numbers and raises no warning whatever text it is given (a closed list: `strlen`, `trim`, `intval` and the like, not `hexdec`, `abs` or `chr`, which warn about text that is no number), an object it may convert, a class name it loads (`method_exists($name, 'm')`, `is_callable('A::b')`, `defined('A::B')`, `class_alias($name, 'B')`, `new ReflectionClass($name)`, `$arrayObject->setIteratorClass($name)`), a class to construct (`$statement->fetchObject('Row')`) or a filter that one of PHP's own `FILTER_…` constants does not name, which may be the one that calls back, or it runs what was registered earlier (an error, session or output-buffer handler, the callbacks of a cURL transfer or an XML parser, an iterator wrapped in another). A warning that a PHP function raises by itself when called directly (`hex2bin` given an odd number of digits, a file that cannot be read) is not counted, although the error handler of the project receives it. This limits every guard form of this specification, not only the ones the flow analysis reads.

- `assert()` is not a guard: assertions are compiled out in production configurations, so the read stays reported. Indirect evidence (a null-coalesced copy tested later) is not followed either.

- E1. Exclude unresolved required symbols, user-defined lookalikes, incomplete syntax, unknown required values and unsupported versions. Cases outside D1 receive no finding.
- E2. Both `@custos-ignore ParseUrlFailureDereferenced` and `@noinspection ParseUrlFailureDereferenced` suppress this native rule.

## Fix

None. A repair requires a semantic decision or application error-handling policy.

## PHP versions

Available in PHP 5.3–8.5 where the referenced API exists. Do not apply extension contracts when the resolved API is unavailable. Gate syntax and version-specific behavior to the configured target.

## Configure

In [`custos.json`](/guide/configuration):

```json
{
  "rules": {
    "ParseUrlFailureDereferenced": {
      "enabled": false
    }
  }
}
```

## Suppress

Before the statement or declaration (or the first statement of the file):

```php
// @custos-ignore ParseUrlFailureDereferenced
```
